analysis:
Examined the three changed files: .github/workflows/darkbloom-watchdog.yml (CI template), changelog.d/darkbloom-watchdog-listing-size.md and docs/developer/build.md. None touches the provider runtime, coordinator WebSocket contract, attestation, App Attest, prefix cache or key custody, so no TB-002/003/007/009/011/012 threat entries or provider assets are affected. T-041 was supplied but is not implicated.

Workflow changes: (1) runs_with/jobs_of now write each page to a file under mktemp -d ($tmp, cleaned by trap) and merge with `jq -cs 'add // []'`. This avoids the jq argv size limit (Argument list too long). The data is GitHub API JSON passed through files or stdin, not interpolated into a shell command, so there is no new injection surface. Failure semantics are kept: a non-200 status returns 1 and callers still exit or continue. One subtle point: `runs_with ... >>$tmp/runs || {...}` and `cancelled=$(runs_with ...)` keep their error handling. (2) The stranded predicate now times each queued Darkbloom job from its own created_at and is suppressed only if a Darkbloom job got a runner within the wait. It no longer considers completion times or other jobs' progress. This is an availability and behavior-policy change: runs with a sibling shard that ran can now be cancelled and re-run on fallback runners, and jobs waiting by design at a payer limit could be cancelled, which the comments and docs now disclose, advising a larger DARKBLOOM_WATCHDOG_MINUTES. It is bounded by the existing at-most-once rescue, the 15..1440 minute validation, max_rescues=2 per round, the marker check, and a GITHUB_TOKEN with only actions:write and checks:write. Re-running on the fallback runners is the intended design and not a trust-boundary change. permissions, token handling, curl --proto =https and the API host check are unchanged. Remaining unverified: the contents of the darkbloom-sandbox upstream template at d6d257c2 (claimed copied unchanged) cannot be checked from the supplied evidence; this is a documentation and provenance matter, not a finding.
